newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark prepares for state selloff.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark prepares for state selloff.

text.p: Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark said on Monday that the state might reduce its 51.73 percent shareholding in the coming months and the board was prepared to buy up to 10 percent of shares on offer in a selloff.
"A reduction of the state's holding could take place in some months' time, including the sale of shares to the company," chairman Knud Heinesen told the group's annual general meeting.

"To ensure full flexibility and to avoid the necessity of an extraordinary general meeting -- if it is agreed that the state should sell shares to the company -- the company, after talks with the state, has found it appropriate that the board authorise the purchase of its own shares," he added.
The government announced in January that it had appointed a working group to assess the value of its Tele Danmark holding but denied that the decision was a direct prelude to further privatisation.
Industry analysts expect a sale in 1998.
